purpose: Test whether explicit first-order latent patch occupancy persistence plus faster conditional cover and imperfect point detection is sufficient to reproduce the Tampa state-dimension memory pattern.

relationship_to_prior_falsifications.new_mechanism: The latent occupied/unoccupied patch state itself persists through time and is only imperfectly observed through finite point samples.

known_truth.latent_occupancy: z[i,t] is a first-order two-state Markov process
known_truth.initial_state: stationary occupancy probability p01 / (1 - p11 + p01)
known_truth.fast_condition: c[i,t] is a site-specific stationary Gaussian AR(1) on the logit scale
known_truth.false_negative: When z=1 but k=0, the coarse recorded state is a non-detection of a truly occupied patch.
known_truth.important_property: Binary and quantitative observations come from the same sampled count; both latent components are first-order. Any older observed-history value is therefore a hidden-state/observation consequence rather than an explicitly higher-order ecological process.

prediction_design.split: Fit each arm once on target years 2-18 and score the unchanged fit separately in heldout target years 19-28.
prediction_design.loss_both_states: mean squared error on common [0,1] scale; binary MSE is Brier score
prediction_design.lag1_model: common baseline + immediately previous observed state
prediction_design.older_history_model: lag1 model + exponentially weighted all-prior observed state
prediction_design.tau_reason: Transferred unchanged from the frozen Tampa coarse-state result and prior mechanism tests.

within_replicate_support_rule.signflip_test: exact one-sided paired sign-flip test of mean target-year MSE delta; p < 0.05
within_replicate_support_rule.lag1_support: Apply rule to lag1 minus baseline.
within_replicate_support_rule.older_history_support: Apply rule to older-history minus lag1.
within_replicate_support_rule.target_pattern: lag1 supported for both binary and quantitative states AND older history supported for binary state AND older history not supported for quantitative state.

cell_support_rule: A cell supports the mechanism when at least 50% of its 32 replicates satisfy the complete target pattern and its median binary-minus-quantitative older-history relative-gain contrast is > 0.

global_support_rule.p11_robustness: Both p11 levels must have at least 12 of their 16 cells satisfy the cell support rule.

secondary_outputs: cell summaries by p11, p01, detectability regime and point count

hard_stop.if_not_supported: Stop response-free mechanism hunting after this v1; retain mechanism as unresolved rather than retuning or adding another simulation family in the same analysis line.
hard_stop.if_supported: Treat as sufficiency only; do not identify latent occupancy persistence as the empirical Tampa mechanism without independent ecological evidence.

forbidden_after_opening: Changing p11, p01, fast-state parameters, point counts or replicate count.
Changing tau, learner, loss, calibration/heldout years or support thresholds.
Adding explicit higher-order ecological memory to rescue failure.
Calling a positive sufficiency result necessary or causal.
interpretation_boundary: A positive result means first-order persistent latent occupancy plus imperfect observation is sufficient to generate the empirical-style memory contrast.
A negative result means thresholding, slow AR(1) suitability, and first-order latent occupancy/detection have all failed as simple sufficiency explanations under their frozen grids.
This is response-free known-truth evidence, not an ecological replication.
